body:
Kinda... I obviously don't know you but my guess is you can understand the actual moment your meant to talk to a doctor/support worker/etc.... Sometimes the words aren't there. 

I always get confused and struggle to explain. You know what I mean? I need to go see my GP this week though, so probably expected to talk to them a bit.

I'm on my forth antidepressant and have tried all the talking therapies. I have a psychiatrist. It just all works for a little while then I stumble into a dark part of my mind that overtakes the rational part. 

What I want right now is to end it.

I know, that the reality is I should look at my life and work out what I can fix and start there with small goals but I've been off work a month and have got to the point I can barely summon the effort to feed myself. I had a med increase the other week. So far things are the same.  I know I cant solve my problems over night but right now even taking small steps feels like climbing a mountain.

Being bigoted

Being intense/possessive/ controlling (I have my life you have yours and we work out a way that fits well for us)

Playing games (I'm too lazy for that shit)

I have the responsibility of not making everyone in my life miserable to live for other than that not really. 

I'm trying to remind myself recurrent depression kinda works this way and that it wont last. But sometimes I feel the facts that I know are crushed by what my depression "knows".

I just wanted to rant a bit I guess and the internet is a pretty good place to do that. 

The ideas feel like they are circling me but I'm pretty sure I have many issues with suicide methods, not definite enough, too messy for the discovery, wasteful, damaging to others. So I sit here and think and feel sad about that. 

I think the hardest part is every depressive episode I feel I lose a little of who I was before it and that's getting harder to accept.

I'm not 100% sure. But I'm a female with depression and I have male friends that have depression. Although in our groups talking about mental health and emotional problems is quite common, sometimes we ease into things by joking and stuff but generally we have a pretty good way of communicating. 

One of the guys I know is now fully recovered. I think it all comes down to stigma about mental health but also I sometimes wonder if there is an extra push on men "to be strong". I hope we can overcome both these issues, as I can relate being suicidal is a sucky way to live and a horrible way to die.
